issue: Under the Mandatory Victims Restitution Act, may a federal court order restitution for psychiatric or psychological care when the victim suffered no bodily injury, or is such care compensable only when the offense resulted in bodily injury?

sides.position: Psychological or psychiatric care is compensable under § 3663A(b)(2) only when the offense resulted in bodily injury to the victim.
cases: United States v. Husky, 924 F.2d 223 (11th Cir. 1991)
United States v. Hicks, 997 F.2d 594 (9th Cir. 1993)
United States v. Manna, 201 F. App'x 146 (4th Cir. 2006)
United States v. Kirkwood, No. 25-50171 (5th Cir. 2026)

sides.position: "Bodily injury" is an umbrella term that can include psychological harm, so psychological care can be ordered under § 3663A(b)(2) even without physical injury; this reading relies on the definition of bodily injury in 18 U.S.C. § 1365(h)(4).
cases: United States v. Breshers, 684 F.3d 696 (7th Cir. 2012)

this_court: requires bodily injury; the Fifth Circuit declines to follow the Seventh Circuit's reasoning and rejects reliance on 18 U.S.C. § 1365(h)(4)
quote: We decline to follow the Seventh Circuit's reasoning.
cite: United States v. Kirkwood, No. 25-50171 (5th Cir. 2026)
